sense: out of the house, out of doors: go out, be out

evidence: Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās
terms.comment: Forās answers “where to?” and forīs “where?”: both are old cases of a noun for door, “out through the door” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: out, outside, out of doors (being out)
evidence: Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.19: cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret
terms.comment: Forīs cēnāre, dine out. Also abroad, in public life, as against domī.

evidence: Plaut. Aul. 40: Exī, inquam. age exī.
terms.comment: English “out” is often the Latin prefix ex-, ē-: exīre, go out; efferre, carry out; ējicere, throw out; ēmittere, let out. “He’s out”, not at home, is abest or forīs est (see away).

phrases.english: Out, I tell you. Come on, out.
Wait, wait: he’s coming out himself.

phrases.latin: vēnit ad nōs Cicerō tuus ad cēnam, cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret
phrases.english: your Cicero came to us for dinner, as Pomponia was dining out

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās; id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre
phrases.english: take care of your health; you will manage that most easily by dining out often

phrases.latin: ut forīs ita domī, ut in magnīs ita in parvīs, ut in aliēnīs ita in suīs agitāre jūstitiam
phrases.english: to practise justice at home as abroad, in small things as in great, in one’s own affairs as in other people’s
